thread:
ana: Heads-up: bringing lucent-v1 (int8) to staging. Quick smoke shows ja->en BLEU drop vs fp16 and a weird token split where ruby/furigana attaches to base kanji differently on quant artifact. Also one RTL sample with Arabic inside parens showed stored paren order flipped.

li: Can you paste a tiny repro and the tokenizer output you saw?

ana: Minimal repro + command:
```
# samples.txt
ja: \u6b63\u6b63\u3001\u30eb\u30d3\u30fc\u306f\u30a2\u30a4\u30c9\u30eb\u3002
rtl_mix: "\u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645(\u05e9\u05dc\u05d5\u05dd)"
python infra/eval/run_eval.py --artifact /artifacts/lucent-v1/int8 --tokenize-only --input samples.txt --out tok.txt
```

ana: tok.txt excerpt (literal escapes):
"\u6b63\u6b63" "\u3001" "\u30eb\u30d3\u30fc" "\u306f" "\u30a2\u30a4\u30c9\u30eb" "\u3002"
"\u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645" "\\u202F(" "\u05e9\u05dc\u05d5\u05dd" ")"

sung: The preserved U+202F between Arabic token and '(' is suspicious. Is fp16 artifact canonicalizing that away?

maria: I ran a quick dev eval on a small ja-en set: fp16 BLEU=35.6, int8 artifact BLEU=31.9. If I point the int8 model at the fp16 tokenizer files (detached tokenizer) BLEU=35.4. So tokenization/detok parity seems dominant.

ci-bot: Created issue ML-2477 "lucent-v1 int8 tokenizer/detok parity (ruby/furigana, U+202F)" and labeled triage, tokenizer, quant.

li: Can you diff normalizer.json from both artifacts? Command: python infra/tokenizer_inspect.py --artifact /artifacts/lucent-v1/fp16 --dump normalizer.json > fp.json; python infra/tokenizer_inspect.py --artifact /artifacts/lucent-v1/int8 --dump normalizer.json > q.json; diff -u fp.json q.json

ana: Ran it. Diff shows int8 packager introduced a rule that preserves ZWSP (U+200B) between CJK and kana and preserves narrow no-break (U+202F) in RTL+paren contexts. fp16 maps U+200B->'' and U+202F->' '. Packager versions differ: fp16 built with packager-2, int8 with packager-4.

sung: Any packaging env differences for bidi handling? PRESERVE_BIDI maybe?

maria: Yes: fp16 artifact set PRESERVE_BIDI=true; int8 packager default used PRESERVE_BIDI=false. detok code calls unicode_bidi_reorder() when preserve_bidi=false which can change stored sequence order. That explains the paren flip.

li: TL;DR: two independent packaging diffs (normalizer rules + PRESERVE_BIDI flag) combined to create token splits and stored-order bidi reorder -> BLEU regression.

ana: Proposed fix: 1) rebuild int8 artifact copying fp16 normalizer.json into quant artifact, 2) set PRESERVE_BIDI=true in packager env for quant builds, 3) add tokenizer parity smoke test in artifact CI that diffs normalizer.json and runs a tiny mixedscript micro-eval (BLEU delta <0.5).

packager-bot: Noted. Opening PKG-204 to investigate packager default changes and add config to pin normalizer behavior.

ci-bot: Marked ML-2477 as blocker-for-int8-onboard and assigned to packaging + eng-ml.

ana: I'll produce a patched int8 artifact with fp16 normalizer + preserve_bidi=true and rerun the ja-en sample; ETA ~30m. Will post numbers.

maria: If you want me to run kernel parity checks afterwards, ping me.

li: Also add an internal doc summarizing why U+200B and U+202F are handled specially for our locales and how PRESERVE_BIDI interacts with detok. Saves future surprises.

ana: Thanks all. Rolling now :thumbsup:
